title: How much aspirin did you get?
hook: 2.00 g of one powder goes in. 1.80 g of aspirin comes out. Is that a 90% yield?

knows: that the limiting reagent sets how much product can form
that a mole is a counted amount
doesNotKnow: that yield is a fraction of the theoretical amount worked out in moles
that starting mass and product mass differ because the molecules weigh differently

misconception: Percent yield is the collected mass divided by the starting mass.
objective: The learner can work out that 2.00 g of salicylic acid is about 0.01448 mol and can make about 2.61 g of aspirin, so collecting 1.80 g is a yield of about 69%, not 90%.

claims.text: The molar mass of salicylic acid is 138.12 g/mol and of aspirin 180.16 g/mol.
claims.source: PubChem: salicylic acid (C7H6O3) 138.12 g/mol; aspirin (C9H8O4) 180.16 g/mol.

claims.text: Salicylic acid reacts with acetic anhydride one mole to one mole to make aspirin; the anhydride is in excess.
claims.source: Standard aspirin synthesis, C7H6O3 + (CH3CO)2O → C9H8O4 + CH3COOH (Vogel's Textbook of Practical Organic Chemistry). 1:1 salicylic acid to aspirin.

claims.text: 2.00 g of salicylic acid is about 0.01448 mol, which can make about 2.61 g of aspirin (the theoretical yield).
Collecting 1.80 g of aspirin is a percent yield of about 69%.
claims.source: 1.80 / 2.6088 = 0.690 (node; Demo.tsx YIELD_PCT). Wrong option: 1.80 / 2.00 = 90% (mass in, mass out).

claims.text: Percent yield is the amount collected divided by the theoretical amount, times 100, with both worked out from the moles of the limiting reagent.
claims.source: IUPAC Gold Book 'yield'; Atkins, Chemical Principles: percent yield = actual yield / theoretical yield × 100.

claims.text: A mole is a counted amount of particles; 138.12 g of salicylic acid is one mole.
claims.source: SI definition of the mole (BIPM SI Brochure, 9th ed.); molar mass is the mass of one mole.

recall.question: 0.100 mol of reactant could make 0.100 mol of product weighing 20.0 g. You collect 15.0 g. The percent yield is…
